title: Feature-Boundary Service Coupling (Cross-Cutting Kitten Delivery)
damaged_code:
```
Adding a new "Kitten Delivery" feature requires modifying:
- Driver Service (to track kitten transport safety)
- Payment Service (to charge the kitten fee)
- Inventory Service (to count available kittens)
- Dispatcher Service (to coordinate kitten pickup)
```
pattern: Decomposing services strictly by functional behavior (e.g., Drivers, Payments, Dispatching) instead of partitioning them around domain-driven bounded contexts.
why_bad: Violates independent deployability. Adding a single, cross-cutting feature forces developers to coordinate, modify, test, and deploy code changes across every single service in the cluster simultaneously, rendering the distributed architecture obsolete.
detection: Observe cases where adding a single business feature requires coordinated commits and deployments across more than 80% of active service repositories.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Highly cohesive pipelines where step-by-step sequential changes are fundamentally required to pass new transaction states.
fix:
Reorganize service boundaries around domain-driven Bounded Contexts where a single team and service can own and deploy the entire lifecycle of a feature.
```
/services/kitten_delivery_service/ // Owns payment, tracking, and dispatch for kitten deliveries
```
source: *Robert C. Martin - Clean Architecture (2017)*, Chapter 27, "Services: Great and Small" (The Kitty Problem / Cross-cutting concerns, p. 242).
